The two grounds are DIFFERENT and this file states the one that holds: docs/close-board-exemptions.json declares `no-truthful-value` because ITS rows are REACHABLE (its own recorded probe returns rc=0) and only the truthfulness of the value bars them, whereas `tools/ledger.py repair` composes `f"{head} {appended} {run}"` and so inserts the appended text BEFORE the canonical run — it cannot displace a token that lives INSIDE it — while the #104 re-declaration refusal blocks a second `rework=`, so the one repair that would clear this leg is unreachable from the moment the collision is written. Reusing the sibling's ground here would assert a reachability this row does not have (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.12, ruling n=3412 PART 6, item 2), so this surface carries its OWN lawful value and refuses every other. The entry is printed as an 'excused:' line on every run, in both invocation modes, so the debt is visible rather than forgiven. The CLASS is now barred at the WRITE path: `tools/ledger.py append` refuses a detail whose canonical run declares the same key more than once, reading the run through the SHARED predicates so the refuser and the detector cannot drift. No second row of this shape can be written at all — this entry is history that no lawful repair reaches, and it is the debt the mechanism retires. Nothing is backfilled: a rewrite of a published detail is a falsified record, not a repair. Skeleton and field rules: docs/audit-rates-exemptions.example.json.

exemptions.domain: the close row's canonical run declares its `rework` disposition twice
exemptions.reason: The close row for #495 (actor hq, ts 2026-10-16T10:13:15Z) was written and pushed in commit 9031129d7f68c80dc355b598241dcf1965c3b2dd with its prose ending `... so the declaration is rework=none.` — the full stop rides INSIDE the value, the token carries `=`, so the positional trailer reader absorbs it into the canonical run beside the trailer's own `rework=none`, and one disposition reads as two. The law gives a row ONE `rework` token (#106, ruling n=386 clause 5). The row is defective and stays exactly as it is: no hand edit, no rewrite of a published detail, no backfill (docs/instruments/ledger.md line 1048). The repair is barred BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by truthfulness, and that distinction is the ground: `cmd_repair` composes the repaired detail as `f"{head} {appended} {run}"`, inserting the appended text BEFORE the canonical run, so it cannot displace a token that lives INSIDE it; and the #104 re-declaration refusal refuses `--append-detail rework=<anything>` against this row, because the run ALREADY declares the key — so the ONE repair that would clear this leg is unreachable from the instant the collision is written. The sibling surface's ground (`no-truthful-value`) does NOT hold here and is not reused (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.12, ruling n=3412 PART 6, item 2). The CLASS is barred at the WRITE path: `tools/ledger.py append` now REFUSES a detail whose canonical run declares the same key more than once, reading the run through the SHARED predicates (`trailer_tokens` and `token_key` in `tools/field_predicate.py`), so no second row of this shape can be written at all. Prevention and repair are not alternatives (#144, ruling n=936; the n=405 precedent as applied at n=2844): this entry repairs what is already written, the refusal prevents the class.
